Vibrant style is a dynamic color mixing scheme provided by SpatialUI. It adjusts the brightness of elements in real time based on the background color and luminance, making it suitable for interfaces that need to maintain readability and visual consistency on complex backgrounds.
## App-level vibrant effect control
You can use the meta-data `com.pico.spatial.ui.isVibrant` to centrally manage the vibrant effect throughout the entire app.

* `true`: Enable vibrant effect. By default, the SDK has enabled vibrant effect for your app.
* `false`: Disable vibrant effect. The app reverts to standard Android 2D rendering. You must manually adapt UI styles to ensure proper display.

After setting this meta-data, you need to restart the app for it to take effect.
```XML
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<manifest xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android">
    <application
        ...>
        <activity 
            ... >
        </activity>
        <meta-data
            android:name="com.pico.spatial.ui.isVibrant"
            android:value="false" />
    </application>
</manifest>
```

## Use pure vibrant mode
In pure vibrant mode, the system dynamically adjusts the brightness of text and other elements according to the vibrant level, implementing rendering effects with visual contrast.
### Vibrant effect levels
Pure vibrant mode provides the following levels of vibrant effect: darkest, ultradark, darker, semidark, dark, neutral, light, semilight, ultralight.
<div style="text-align: center"><img src="https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/f87d78b2a6f84e6194126214c9f40fa4~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image" width="3200px" /></div>

### Usage
SpatialUI provides a special color value `Color.Vibrant`. Use it together with `Modifier.vibrantEffect` to enable pure vibrant mode. For example:
```Kotlin
Box( 
    modifier = Modifier.size(100.dp)
        .vibrantEffect(Vibrant.Neutral)
        .bacground(Color.Vibrant)
)
```

The final rendering is as follows:
![Image](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/92b83992654444da884b201f1dc3727a~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image)
You can also use pure vibrant mode to render text. Note that the `vibrant` parameter of the `Text` component takes precedence over `Modifier.vibrantEffect`.
```Kotlin
// The priority of the Text component's vibrant is higher than Modifier.vibrantEffect
Text("Hello", color = Color.Vibrant, vibrant = Vibrant.Neutral)
// Or
Text("Hello", color = Color.Vibrant, modifier = Modifier.vibrantEffect(Vibrant.Neutral))
```

### Limitations
The limitations of pure vibrant mode are as follows:

* Only supports rendering monochrome scenes, such as monochrome backgrounds and text.
* Does not support rendering images.
* Does not support gradient colors.
* When pure vibrant mode is disabled and reverts to Android 2D rendering, `Color.Vibrant` will appear black. Do not use this color value outside of vibrant mode.

## Blend vibrant effect with solid colors
After enabling vibrant mode, regular colors can be blended with different levels of vibrant effect.
### Blending rules
The following table provides a comparison of rendering effects between "pure vibrant mode" and "vibrant effect blended with solid colors":
| **Vibrant** | **Color** | **Rendering** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| None <br>  | `Color.Vibrant`: <br> ![Image](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/c390cdc064ed497b8bf7c9c9f64cfa1c~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) | Pure vibrant effect, and the background is pure black. <br> ![Image](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/c390cdc064ed497b8bf7c9c9f64cfa1c~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) |
| Yes, for example `Vibrant.Light`: <br> ![Image](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/37e04ebe019945a6be09b5d5d7a18d74~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) | `Color.Vibrant`: <br> ![Image](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/c390cdc064ed497b8bf7c9c9f64cfa1c~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) | Pure light-level vibrant effect. Actual rendering may vary. <br> ![Image](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/37e04ebe019945a6be09b5d5d7a18d74~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) |
| None | Regular color value, such as `Color.red`: <br> ![Image](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/deaeb5fc6a0347e9acfdd9ec2178a471~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) | Regular red. <br> ![Image](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/deaeb5fc6a0347e9acfdd9ec2178a471~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) |
| Yes, for example `Vibrant.Light`: <br> ![Image](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/37e04ebe019945a6be09b5d5d7a18d74~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) | Regular color value, such as `Color.red`: <br> ![Image](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/deaeb5fc6a0347e9acfdd9ec2178a471~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) | `Vibrant.Light` blended with `Color.red`. Actual rendering may vary. <br> ![Image](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/b979766875234284951b79529c94308b~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) |
### Usage
In `Modifier.vibrantEffect()`, set a level for vibrant effect, then set the background color in `Modifier.background()`. The code sample is as follows:
```Kotlin
Box( 
    modifier = Modifier.size(100.dp)
        .vibrantEffect(Vibrant.Light)
        .bacground(Color.Red)
)
```

## Vibrant effect propagation
### Propagate vibrant effect
In Compose, `RenderNode` is organized in a tree structure. When vibrant effect is enabled on a node, all its child nodes will inherit that vibrant effect by default, until it is replaced by a new vibrant effect or explicitly terminated.
```Kotlin
Box(
    modifier = Modifier
        .background(Color.Green) // Pure green background, no vibrant effect
        .vibrantEffect(Vibrant.Light) // Enable vibrant effect
        .border(1.dp, Color.Vibrant)  // Pure vibrant border
        .drawBehind {
            drawXXX()  // Render in vibrant mode
        }
) {
    Box(
        modifier = Modifier
            .background(Color.Blue) // Blend the light-level vibrant effect with Blue color, Vibrant.Light is inherited from the parent node
    )
    Text("Hello", color = Color.Vibrant)) // Text: Pure light-level vibrant effect, Vibrant.Light is inherited from the parent node
}
```

### Replace vibrant effect
In the rendering pipeline, you can replace the previous vibrant effect by setting `Modifier.vibrantEffect()` again. Subsequent nodes will be rendered using the latest vibrant effect. 
```Kotlin
Box(
    modifier = Modifier
        .vibrantEffect(Virant.Light)
        .background(Color.Virbrant)  // The background has the light-level vibrant effect
        .vibrantEffect(Vibrant.Dark)
        .border(1.dp,Color.Red)  // The border has the dark-level vibrant effect
) {
    Text("Hello", color = Color.Vibrant)) // The text has the dark-level vibrant effect, which is inherited from the last vibrant effect of the parent node
}
```

### Terminate the propagation of vibrant effect
If you want to use vibrant effect only for the background, while rendering child nodes with solid colors, you can call `Modifier.terminationVibrantEffect()` at the appropriate node, or set the node's `Modifier.vibrant()` to `Vibrant.Termination` to terminate the propagation of vibrant effect.
For example, you can directly terminate the propagation of the parent node's vibrant effect for all subsequent child nodes.
```Kotlin
Box(
    modifier = Modifier
        .vibrantEffect(Virant.Light)  // Vibrant effect is enabled for the forbackground
        .background(Color.Virbrant)    
        .terminationVibrantEffect()  // Terminate vibrant effect, subsequent nodes will not be rendered in vibrant effect
) {
    Text("Hello", color = Color.Red)) // Since the parent node terminated the vibrant effect, the text is rendered with a solid color
}
```

For example, you can terminate the propagation of the parent node's vibrant effect for some child nodes, while enabling a new vibrant effect for them.
```Kotlin
Column(
    modifier = Modifier
        .vibrantEffect(Virant.Light)  // Vibrant effect is enabled for the background
        .background(Color.Virbrant)   
) {
    // Terminate vibrant effect at the current node; this text will be rendered entirely by Android 2D
    Text("Hello", color = Color.Red, virbant = Vibrant.Termination)  
    // Because vibrant effect is enabled for the parent node, this text has an inherited light-level vibrant effect, and the vibrant effect is blended with color red
    Text("Hello", color = Color.Red)  
    // You can also use new vibrant effect to render child nodes, for example, enabling the dark-level Vibrant effect for this tex
    Text("Hello", color = Color.Red, vibrant = Vibrant.Dark) 
}
```

## Monitor whether the current node has vibrant effect
SpatialUI provides two ways to determine whether the current node has vibrant effect:

* **Explicit setting**: If you directly call `Modifier.vibrantEffect()`, then the node must have vibrant effect.
* **Propagation detection**: The vibrant effect of the parent node can be propagated to its child nodes. You can use the `observeCurrentVibrantEffect` method to monitor the status of the current node's vibrant effect in real time.
   ```Kotlin
   @Composable
   fun ObserveVibrantSample() {
       Column(
           modifier =
               Modifier.size(200.dp)
                   // Enable the dark-level vibrant effect
                   .vibrantEffect(Vibrant.Dark)
       ) {
           Column(modifier = Modifier.background(Color.Red)) {
               var currentVibrant by remember { mutableStateOf<Vibrant?>(null) }
               Box(
                   modifier =
                       Modifier
                           // Monitor the status of vibrant effect for the current node
                           .observeCurrentVibrantEffect { currentVibrant = it },
               )
               Text(
                   "current vibrant is: $currentVibrant",
                   color = Color.Yellow,
               )
           }
       }
   }
   ```


## API reference
The `Vibrant` provides functions and enumerations for managing vibrant effect settings. For more information, refer to the API reference.
